options.metric: Annual sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed across crash records
options.denominator: None (absolute total, not a rate); all in-scope crash rows contribute their nonmissing recorded pedestrian-killed count
options.grouping: Calendar year derived from crash_date, 2013 through 2025
options.reason: An annual absolute total directly answers how many recorded pedestrian deaths occurred and preserves the requested year-by-year comparison.
options.interpretation: For 2013–2025, the chart gives the requested annual totals by summing each crash row's number_of_pedestrians_killed and assigning the crash to the calendar year of crash_date; the plotted totals range from 101 in 2020 to 176 in 2013. An absolute sum of people killed is a direct measure of how many pedestrian deaths were recorded, rather than a crash-normalized rate. It cannot establish whether every pedestrian death is represented beyond the supplied police-reported NYC crash file. The checks found 0 missing crash_date values before the year filter, 0 missing pedestrian-killed values in every target year, and full Jan–Dec date coverage in all years, so no target rows were dropped or counted differently.
